excerpts: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on the four-dimensional affine Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, as in the selected HEFT spacetime convention. Use the trivial spin structure, spinor bundle $S=M\times\mathbb C^4$, gamma matrices satisfying $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$, chirality operator $\gamma_5=-i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3=i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, and eigensubbundles $S_\pm=\ker(\gamma_5\mp I)$. Here $\gamma_0=-\gamma^0$, $\gamma_j=\gamma^j$ for spatial $j$, and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger i\gamma^0$; choose $(i\gamma^0)^\dagger=i\gamma^0$ and $(\gamma^j)^\dagger=\gamma^j$. This matches the shared anomaly-matching data and Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention in Eq. (2.20), which fixes the sign of his anomaly formula. Take the trivial bundle for the fixed global symmetry group $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, set the $SU(3)$ background connection to zero, and keep only the nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B\in\Omega_c^1(M,\mathbb R)$ with curvature $G=dB$. Here $U(1)_V=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ and its charge-$q$ representation is $\rho_q(z)=z^q$ on $\mathbb C$. The background $B$ is not integrated over as a quantum gauge redundancy.

excerpts: On natural-unit Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, take the trivial $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ bundle, zero $SU(3)$ background, and a smooth compactly supported real nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ with $G=dB$. Let $\alpha,\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. Use the model's source-signed chirality convention $\gamma_5=-i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3=i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, with positive chirality meaning eigenvalue $+1$. Use one smooth compactly supported positive-chirality Weyl field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$, one smooth compactly supported neutral negative-chirality mass partner, and the charge-one scalar $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ in the Yukawa term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where $v>0$, $y\ne0$, and $M_H=|y|v$. Fix the transformations $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$, and use the consistent-anomaly representative with no non-invariant local counterterm. For any fixed integer $n\geq1$, consider a specified $n$-point background-field vertex of $\Gamma_H$ with insertions from components of $B$ and/or $\theta$, and incoming real coordinate covectors $p_j=(p_{j0},p_{j1},p_{j2},p_{j3})\in\mathbb R^{1,3}$ satisfying $\sum_{j=1}^n p_j=0$; set $E=\max_{1\leq j\leq n,\,0\leq\mu\leq3}|p_{j\mu}|$. No on-shell condition is imposed. Require $E/M_H\ll1$ only for the low-energy effective-field-theory interpretation of that vertex. This condition applies to its finite set of external legs, not to the Fourier support of the compactly supported backgrounds, and gives no expansion-remainder bound; the exact local anomaly identity below is independent of it.

excerpts: In the trivial-bundle $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ threshold model on natural-unit Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and zero $SU(3)$ background, use a smooth real compactly supported $U(1)_V$ potential $B$ and parameter $\alpha$, with $G=dB$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. Choose a smooth compactly supported cutoff $\chi$ that equals $1$ on a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\alpha$, with $\alpha\geq0$. Let $\lambda>0$ have mass dimension two and set $B=\lambda\chi(x)(x^0dx^1+x^2dx^3)$, normalizing $\alpha$ so that $\lambda^2\int_M\alpha\,d^4x=1$. For the charge-one positive-chirality field, neutral mass partner, and $M_H>0$ of the stated formal model, this evaluates the exact local identity from the preceding theorem. It makes no assertion about a finite-momentum vertex or the Fourier support of the chosen compactly supported backgrounds. The consistent heavy-sector and Wess–Zumino variations are equal, nonzero, and each equal $+1/(12\pi^2)$.
